gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-004 concerns the box-dimension definition allowing a positive limiting mesh size and consequent scale dependence. It does not identify the distinct invalid fixed-n_2 inner-limit equality replacing neighborhood cover counts by exact-spectrum counts, nor the insufficiency of the factor-three estimate to yield equality.

Both diagnose that finite operator support does not imply finite neighborhoods in the independently specified graph, so the universally asserted finite-layer breadth-first construction is not defined. ISSUE-012 additionally identifies the separate connectivity/exhaustiveness ambiguity, while its core diagnosis exactly covers the gold defect.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The graph assumptions do not establish local finiteness of the graph used by the breadth-first construction: finite nonzero operator support or row support does not imply finitely many graph neighbors. Consequently a permitted infinite-neighborhood graph can make the finite q_1/layer construction fail.

component_coverage.gold_component: The finite-support assumptions constrain operator couplings but do not imply that the independently given graph has finitely many neighbors; an admitted infinite-star example therefore prevents the asserted finite-layer breadth-first procedure from beginning.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly states that finite operator support does not imply local finiteness of the given graph, supplies an admitted graph with an infinite first neighborhood, and concludes that the breadth-first construction is not defined for the full class.
